title: Using codex, I made an app where your workouts give you points to level up your character
author: ssj4gogeta78
selftext:
Hey everyone, I'd love to get some feedback on a project I've been working on.

I'm very new to app and game development, but over the past few months I've been building an iOS workout tracker, and about a month ago I decided to gamify the entire experience. The app is called Swole Streets (available for free on the iOS App Store).

I drew a lot of inspiration from games like Castle Crashers and Super Mario Bros, as well as anime like Solo Leveling. I created basically all of the art myself, and relied heavily on Codex to build out the coding, core mechanics and internal logic.

Every time you log a workout (weight training, stretching, sports, etc.), you earn 1 stat point. You can assign points to Health, Damage, Magic, Speed, or Special Ability (capped at 3 points per day).Reaching workout milestones levels up your character, giving a +1 boost to all stats.

Questions that could help me:

1. Do you think the hybrid "retro workout tracker + arcade game" model works as something to play between sets or in your spare time, or would it be better to split them up and focus purely on the game?
2. Is the concept engaging enough to keep you motivated to log daily workouts? Is there something i can do to make it more engaging?
3. Is the game too simple? Like would better art be more captivating or is the simple vibe better?

I'd love to hear your thoughts, critical feedback, or ideas on what to do with this concept.

More info on the project website: [Todd Labs](https://todd-labs.github.io/todd-legal/index.html)

comments.author: Ok-Design6467
comments.body: I like the aesthetic! I’m kinda confused though, is it a workout app or a game? Where am I supposed to track my workouts?

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body:
I've thought a lot about tying fitness with gaming so this topic interests me. I even prototyped a physical workout card game with dice rolling. Kind of fun actually and a good workout. I made an app for myself that gives me workouts and will have random bonus points for completing extra reps. It even has a little shop for buying outfits to deck out your dinosaur avatar with points you earn from completing workout missions. But it's not a game on its own like yours is.  
  
As for your idea, honestly, the game portion looks really weak for me to want to keep playing. But, the best way to know is to test it out yourself. Is the game fun for YOU? Do some workouts and see if you want to play a retro arcade game during a rest when you're huffing and sweating. If you like it, then great. Keep going. I think what matters is if you try it and feel there is something there. If you think, gosh, I can't wait to log another workout so I can go beat that boss with the extra stat point, then maybe you have something. As it stands now, I doubt this retro arcade game has enough of a hook. But that's why you test and iterate. I think your goal should be to create that experience where you can't wait to get another workout in. Hell, you could throw loot box into the mix and make it addictive. People by nature love the gambling rush and a loot box might be way more compelling than just a measly stat point.

replies.author: ssj4gogeta78
replies.body: Thank you so much for the genuine feedback! I definitely see what you are saying, and I agree. I have been thinking of what I can do to the game to make it feel more captivating. I love those arcade style games, but I think there is something (or a lot of somethings) that my game could use to make it more enticing. I'll try to keep brainstorming on how I can make the user more thrilled to log workouts. Thanks again!
